newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Hutu rebels clash with Burundi army near capital.
newsitem.headline: Hutu rebels clash with Burundi army near capital.

text.p: Hundreds of people were fleeing their homes south of Burundi's capital on Tuesday after fierce fighting between Hutu rebels and the Tutsi-dominated army, witnesses said.
They said fighting broke out about 15 km (nine miles) south of Bujumburu in the afternoon and was continuing as night fell.
Witnesses heard the sound of mortar and gun fire and saw hundreds of local residents packing up their belongings to head for the capital.
"It seems the aim of the rebels is to try cut off national route seven," said one witness referring to the highway that links the capital to the south.
Other witnesses in the outskirts of the capital said mortar fire could be heard in the late afternoon.
An army spokesman said government troops had earlier killed 30 rebels and seized seven weapons in fighting to the east of the capital.
He said the army was carrying out an operation there to flush rebels out of the area.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since Burundi's first elected Hutu president was assassinated by troops in 1993.
